title: Specific heat
target: Use mass, material and temperature change to calculate heating energy.
criteria: Identify ΔT rather than final temperature alone.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: A sample warms from −8°C to 7°C without phase change. What temperature change belongs in Q = mcΔT?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A student uses 42°C as ΔT when a sample warms from 31°C to 42°C. What is the corrected ΔT?
cpa.guide: Use the change, 42 − 31 = 11°C, not the final reading.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.

cpa.prompt: A 0.50 kg sample with c = 800 J/(kg·°C) warms by 6°C. What heat input is required without losses?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A 250 g sample has c = 400 J/(kg·°C) and warms by 8°C. What is Q?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: Equal masses A and B receive equal heat with no phase change. A has twice B’s specific heat. Compare temperature rises.
cpa.guide: ΔT is inversely proportional to c for the same energy and mass.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.

cpa.prompt: A 0.20 kg model sample needs 360 J to warm by 3°C. What specific heat fits the data?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.
